headline: Zach Yadegari, the teenage co-founder of the calorie-tracking app Cal AI, has launched an AI assistant start-up called Persona and raised $10 million.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 5: a small round and an early product, with claims that come from the founder.
importance_line: What changed is that another consumer AI assistant with its own wearable is entering a crowded field, which matters to people considering handing shopping and errands to an AI that keeps data in the cloud, then to rivals such as Meta's Muse assistant, and the doubt is that the privacy, advertising-neutrality and preorder claims are the founder's own.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Persona, led by Yadegari after he left MyFitnessPal, which bought Cal AI in March, raised $10 million led by Vine Ventures and plans a $179 wearable band in December that is activated by a button or a wrist flick and is not always listening. Persona's model runs in its cloud and its business currently relies on ads shown during shopping research, though Yadegari says the agent will not know which products are advertised.
